# THEORYs with `tags` `altruism`

**Altruism and self-interest** — whether and how action can aim at another's good rather than one's own — psychological egoism and its rivals, the empathy–altruism debate and self–other merging, inclusion of others in the self and identity fusion, team reasoning and group-directed preferences, identity in the utility function, the evolution of unselfish behaviour (kin, reciprocal and group selection), and the extent of the self as it bears on what counts as self-interest (ADR-062).

| [THEORY-655](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-655.md) v3 | Social behaviour evolves as if each individual valued a neighbour's fitness against its own by their coefficient of relationship, and its discriminations evolve to make that coefficient determinate; so kin are favoured and strangers met with hostility, relatives fight less, and haplodiploid sisters, related by 3/4, are predisposed to worker altruism | Hamilton (1964), Part II, [LIT-506](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-506.md), read in full in [NOTE-410](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-410.md), on Part I's model ([LIT-497](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-497.md)). Two general principles, offered as an "unrigorous" generalization, are applied to alarm calls, kin recognition in gulls and terns, clones and colonies, Hymenoptera, and fights. The evidence is anecdotal. The author calls his positive indications for distant relatives "rather few and feeble", reports Australian halictines and multiple mating as running against the hymenopteran hypothesis, and explains anomalies case by case. | Proposed |
